text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.

GERMANY - German Bunds extend losses in late afternoon trade as market bacame convinced no more German rate cuts were likely in the near term and U.S. prices dipped. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.18, down 0.29 from Wednesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - British gilts sank as dips in bunds and sliding sterling outweighed positive sentiment from a successful auction of long-dated stock. Dealers said solid support for Dec gilt futures around 109-04. Market looking to Q3 GDP and trade data on Friday. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-05/32, down 20/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - December bond future settled near 126.16 support, driven lower by bunds. Franc and rate cut hopes helped PIBOR. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 126.22, down 0.16 from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures dipped slightly lower in late afternoon with traders watching the easier trend in bund and T-bonds. Some profit-taking persisted after the Italian discount rate cut late Wednesday. The market took little support from the lira which perked up, supported by a steady dollar. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 123.26, down 0.22 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - US Treasuries were at session lows at mid-morning after an unexpectedly sharp drop in weekly jobless claims to 320,000 hinted at a tightening labour market. Seasonal factors, particularly the Columbus Day holiday in the survey week, was seen as having played a role in the decline.The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 110-14/32, down 13/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.87 percent.

JAPAN - The December Japanese government bond futures contract ended higher, time high for any benchmark contract of 124.42 in the afternoon. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 124.53, up 0.63 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Five-year dollar bonds continued to surface in the Eurobond market, with two deals launched on Thursday. Associates Corp set a $600 million five-year deal, which will be priced to yield 40 b.p. over TreasuCo brought a $300 million five-year bond at 222 b.p. over Treasuries. Credit Local added 100 billion lire to a 10-year bondlaunched on Wednesday.
